# Contract: List Tasks

*Generated by spec-writer. Hand edits are overwritten on regeneration.*

## Prerequisites

These conditions describe the environment in which items in this
contract are exercised. Producing them is part of the feature's
deliverable, alongside the implementation itself — a contract whose
prerequisites are not yet satisfied is not failing, it is still being
built. Once the feature is delivered, any missing condition halts item
execution until it is restored.

**Runtime services:**
- a PostgreSQL 16 server is reachable at the `DATABASE_URL` provided by `.env.test`, and its role can create and drop databases (each item runs against its own isolated database)
- the `task-api` service built from this repository is available both as an in-process router and as a spawnable binary (`cargo run` or the compiled `task-api` executable)
- a Rust stable toolchain ≥ 1.100 with the `rustfmt` and `clippy` components is installed

**Persistent state:**
- `migrated-db` — a PostgreSQL database exists on which every migration shipped so far has been applied exactly once with matching checksums; the `tasks` table exists and holds zero rows unless an item's `given` adds rows. Used by: API-PAGE-01, API-PAGE-08, API-QUERY-01, API-QUERY-02, API-QUERY-03, API-QUERY-04, API-QUERY-05, API-QUERY-06, API-QUERY-07, API-QUERY-08, API-QUERY-09, API-QUERY-10, API-QUERY-11, API-QUERY-12, API-QUERY-13, API-QUERY-14, API-QUERY-15, API-QUERY-16, API-REJECT-01, API-REJECT-02.
- `twenty-five-tasks` — `migrated-db` holds exactly 25 tasks titled `Task 01` … `Task 25` (two-digit numbering), created one at a time in numeric order so that `created_at` strictly increases from `Task 01` to `Task 25`; every other field may take any valid value. Used by: API-PAGE-02, API-PAGE-03, API-PAGE-04, API-PAGE-05, API-PAGE-06.
- `tied-tasks` — `migrated-db` holds exactly 20 tasks that all have `status` `todo`, `priority` `medium`, `due_date` NULL and one identical `created_at` (equal to their `updated_at`). Used by: API-PAGE-07, API-SORT-07.
- `mixed-tasks` — `migrated-db` holds exactly the 9 tasks below, created one at a time in the listed order so that `created_at` strictly increases down the table and each `updated_at` equals its `created_at`. Used by: API-FILTER-01, API-FILTER-02, API-FILTER-03, API-FILTER-04, API-FILTER-05, API-FILTER-06, API-SORT-01, API-SORT-02, API-SORT-03, API-SORT-04, API-SORT-05, API-SORT-06.

  | # | title | status | priority | due_date |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | `T-todo-low` | `todo` | `low` | `2026-12-05` |
  | 2 | `T-todo-medium` | `todo` | `medium` | NULL |
  | 3 | `T-todo-high` | `todo` | `high` | `2026-12-01` |
  | 4 | `T-prog-low` | `in_progress` | `low` | NULL |
  | 5 | `T-prog-medium` | `in_progress` | `medium` | `2026-12-03` |
  | 6 | `T-prog-high` | `in_progress` | `high` | `2026-12-07` |
  | 7 | `T-done-low` | `done` | `low` | `2026-12-02` |
  | 8 | `T-done-medium` | `done` | `medium` | `2026-12-06` |
  | 9 | `T-done-high` | `done` | `high` | NULL |

- `seeded-10k-db` — a migrated PostgreSQL database whose `tasks` table holds exactly 10,000 rows with statuses and priorities spread across every allowed value (at least 100 rows with `status` `todo`) and about one third of `due_date` values NULL. Used by: API-PERF-01.

**Configuration:**
- `.env.test` at the repository root defines `DATABASE_URL` for the PostgreSQL 16 server above, and its variables are present in the environment of `cargo test`
- unless an item states otherwise: `HOST=127.0.0.1`, `PORT=<a free TCP port>`, `DATABASE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=10`, `DATABASE_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECS=5`, `DATABASE_URL` pointing to the item's database, `ENABLE_TEST_ROUTES` unset
- `ENABLE_TEST_ROUTES=true` mounts the diagnostic route `GET /__test/slow?ms=<0..30000>[&hold_db=true]`, used only by `API-REJECT-01` to hold the database pool's only connection; when the flag is unset or `false`, that path behaves as an unknown route
- `<invalid-query body>(<entries>)` denotes the exact body `{"error":{"code":"invalid_query","message":"Query parameters are invalid","details":[<entries>]}}`, where `<entries>` is the listed sequence of `{"field":…,"message":…}` objects
- the `tasks` table can be read directly with SQL (outside the service) so items can assert stored rows

## Quality gates

Each gate must pass for the feature to be considered ready.

- **Format** — `cargo fmt --check` — every source file is already rustfmt-formatted; the command exits 0 with no diff.
- **Lint** — `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — all targets (library, binary, tests) compile with zero clippy warnings.
- **Tests** — `cargo test` — every unit and integration test passes against isolated `#[sqlx::test]` databases on the PostgreSQL server named by `.env.test`.
- **Offline build** — `SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo build` — the project compiles from the committed `.sqlx/` metadata without contacting a database.

## Coverage Manifest

| PRD Acceptance Criterion | Covered by |
|---|---|
| `GET /tasks` on an empty database returns `{"items":[],"total":0,"limit":20,"offset":0}`. | API-PAGE-01 |
| With 25 tasks, `GET /tasks` returns 20 items ordered by `created_at` descending with `total: 25`, and `?offset=20` returns the remaining 5. | API-PAGE-02, API-PAGE-03 |
| `?status=todo,in_progress` returns only tasks with those statuses, and `total` reflects the filtered count. | API-FILTER-01, API-FILTER-06 |
| `?status=todo&priority=high` returns only tasks matching both conditions. | API-FILTER-02, API-FILTER-05 |
| `?sort=priority&order=desc` returns all `high` tasks before `medium` before `low`. | API-SORT-01 |
| `?sort=due_date&order=asc` and `?sort=due_date&order=desc` both place tasks with a `null` due date last. | API-SORT-03, API-SORT-04 |
| Tasks with identical sort values are ordered by `id` ascending, and paging through all results with `limit=7` returns every task exactly once. | API-SORT-07, API-PAGE-07 |
| `?limit=0`, `?limit=101`, `?offset=-1`, `?offset=10001`, `?status=closed`, `?sort=title`, and `?order=up` each return 400 `invalid_query` naming the parameter. | API-QUERY-01, API-QUERY-02, API-QUERY-03, API-QUERY-04, API-QUERY-05, API-QUERY-06, API-QUERY-07 |
| A request with 2 invalid parameters returns a single 400 with 2 `details` entries. | API-QUERY-08, API-QUERY-13 |
| `?offset=1000` with 25 tasks returns `items: []` and `total: 25`. | API-PAGE-04 |
| p95 latency < 100 ms for `?status=todo&sort=due_date&limit=100` with 10,000 seeded tasks (release build, local). | API-PERF-01 |

## HTTP API

**Verification mode:** Send an HTTP request to the running service (in-process router or bound listener); assert response status, headers and body, and response time where stated.

### Paginate

**Common given:** the service is running against `migrated-db`.

#### `API-PAGE-01` — empty database returns an empty default page
- given: (default), and `tasks` holds zero rows
- when: GET /tasks
- then:
  - status 200
  - header `Content-Type` is `application/json`
  - body is exactly `{"items":[],"total":0,"limit":20,"offset":0}`

#### `API-PAGE-02` — default page holds the 20 newest tasks
- given: (default), and `twenty-five-tasks` exists
- when: GET /tasks
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` has 20 entries whose titles are `Task 25`, `Task 24`, …, `Task 06`, in that order
  - body `total` is 25
  - body `limit` is 20
  - body `offset` is 0

#### `API-PAGE-03` — offset returns the remaining tasks
- given: (default), and `twenty-five-tasks` exists
- when: GET /tasks?offset=20
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` has 5 entries whose titles are `Task 05`, `Task 04`, `Task 03`, `Task 02`, `Task 01`, in that order
  - body `total` is 25
  - body `offset` is 20

#### `API-PAGE-04` — offset beyond total returns no items
- given: (default), and `twenty-five-tasks` exists
- when: GET /tasks?offset=1000
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` is `[]`
  - body `total` is 25
  - body `offset` is 1000

#### `API-PAGE-05` — smallest page size is accepted
- given: (default), and `twenty-five-tasks` exists
- when: GET /tasks?limit=1
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` has exactly one entry, titled `Task 25`
  - body `limit` is 1
  - body `total` is 25

#### `API-PAGE-06` — largest page size and offset are accepted
- given: (default), and `twenty-five-tasks` exists
- when: GET /tasks?limit=100&offset=10000
- then:
  - status 200
  - body is exactly `{"items":[],"total":25,"limit":100,"offset":10000}`

#### `API-PAGE-07` — paging with limit 7 visits every task exactly once
- given: (default), and `tied-tasks` exists
- when: GET /tasks?limit=7&offset=0, then GET /tasks?limit=7&offset=7, then GET /tasks?limit=7&offset=14
- then:
  - every response has status 200
  - every response body `total` is 20
  - the three pages hold 7, 7 and 6 items
  - the 20 returned ids are pairwise distinct and are exactly the ids of `tied-tasks`
  - the concatenated ids are in ascending order

#### `API-PAGE-08` — list items use the task representation from create
- given: (default), `tasks` holds zero rows, and `POST /tasks` with `Content-Type: application/json` and body `{"title":"Write PRD","priority":"high","due_date":"2026-12-01"}` has returned 201 with body `created-body`
- when: GET /tasks
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` has exactly one entry
  - that entry is equal, as JSON, to `created-body`
  - body `total` is 1

### Filter

**Common given:** the service is running against `migrated-db`; `mixed-tasks` exists.

#### `API-FILTER-01` — several statuses combine with OR
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?status=todo,in_progress
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` has 6 entries
  - every entry's `status` is `todo` or `in_progress`
  - body `total` is 6

#### `API-FILTER-02` — status and priority combine with AND
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?status=todo&priority=high
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` has exactly one entry, titled `T-todo-high`
  - body `total` is 1

#### `API-FILTER-03` — several priorities combine with OR
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?priority=low,high
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` has 6 entries
  - every entry's `priority` is `low` or `high`
  - body `total` is 6

#### `API-FILTER-04` — a repeated value inside a list is accepted
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?status=done,done
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` has 3 entries
  - every entry's `status` is `done`
  - body `total` is 3

#### `API-FILTER-05` — filters, sort and limit combine
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?status=todo,in_progress&priority=high&sort=due_date&order=asc&limit=50
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` titles are `T-todo-high`, `T-prog-high`, in that order
  - body `total` is 2
  - body `limit` is 50

#### `API-FILTER-06` — total counts every match regardless of limit
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?status=todo,in_progress&limit=2
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` has 2 entries
  - body `total` is 6

### Sort

**Common given:** the service is running against `migrated-db`; `mixed-tasks` exists.

#### `API-SORT-01` — priority sorts semantically, descending
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?sort=priority&order=desc
- then:
  - status 200
  - entries 1–3 of `items` have `priority` `high`
  - entries 4–6 have `priority` `medium`
  - entries 7–9 have `priority` `low`

#### `API-SORT-02` — priority sorts semantically, ascending
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?sort=priority&order=asc
- then:
  - status 200
  - entries 1–3 of `items` have `priority` `low`
  - entries 4–6 have `priority` `medium`
  - entries 7–9 have `priority` `high`

#### `API-SORT-03` — ascending due date puts undated tasks last
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?sort=due_date&order=asc
- then:
  - status 200
  - entries 1–6 of `items` are titled `T-todo-high`, `T-done-low`, `T-prog-medium`, `T-todo-low`, `T-done-medium`, `T-prog-high`, in that order
  - entries 7–9 have `due_date` `null`
  - entries 7–9 are in ascending `id` order

#### `API-SORT-04` — descending due date also puts undated tasks last
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?sort=due_date&order=desc
- then:
  - status 200
  - entries 1–6 of `items` are titled `T-prog-high`, `T-done-medium`, `T-todo-low`, `T-prog-medium`, `T-done-low`, `T-todo-high`, in that order
  - entries 7–9 have `due_date` `null`
  - entries 7–9 are in ascending `id` order

#### `API-SORT-05` — ascending order defaults to creation time
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?order=asc
- then:
  - status 200
  - `items` titles are the 9 `mixed-tasks` titles in table order (`T-todo-low` first, `T-done-high` last)

#### `API-SORT-06` — update time can be sorted descending
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?sort=updated_at&order=desc
- then:
  - status 200
  - `items` titles are the 9 `mixed-tasks` titles in reverse table order (`T-done-high` first, `T-todo-low` last)

#### `API-SORT-07` — identical sort values are ordered by id ascending
- given: the service is running against `migrated-db`; `tied-tasks` exists
- when: GET /tasks?sort=priority&order=desc&limit=100
- then:
  - status 200
  - body `items` has 20 entries
  - the entries' ids are in strictly ascending order

### Query Validation

**Common given:** the service is running against `migrated-db`; `tasks` holds zero rows.

#### `API-QUERY-01` — limit of 0 is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?limit=0
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"limit","message":"must be an integer between 1 and 100"})`

#### `API-QUERY-02` — limit of 101 is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?limit=101
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"limit","message":"must be an integer between 1 and 100"})`

#### `API-QUERY-03` — negative offset is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?offset=-1
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"offset","message":"must be an integer between 0 and 10000"})`

#### `API-QUERY-04` — offset of 10001 is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?offset=10001
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"offset","message":"must be an integer between 0 and 10000"})`

#### `API-QUERY-05` — unknown status value is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?status=closed
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"status","message":"must be one of: todo, in_progress, done"})`

#### `API-QUERY-06` — unknown sort field is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?sort=title
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"sort","message":"must be one of: created_at, updated_at, due_date, priority"})`

#### `API-QUERY-07` — unknown order is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?order=up
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"order","message":"must be one of: asc, desc"})`

#### `API-QUERY-08` — two invalid parameters are reported together
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?status=closed&limit=500
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"status","message":"must be one of: todo, in_progress, done"},{"field":"limit","message":"must be an integer between 1 and 100"})`

#### `API-QUERY-09` — every invalid parameter is reported in a fixed order
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?offset=x&limit=x&order=x&sort=x&priority=x&status=x
- then:
  - status 400
  - body `error.code` is `invalid_query`
  - body `error.details` has 6 entries whose `field` values are `status`, `priority`, `sort`, `order`, `limit`, `offset`, in that order

#### `API-QUERY-10` — unknown priority value is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?priority=urgent
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"priority","message":"must be one of: low, medium, high"})`

#### `API-QUERY-11` — non-integer limit is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?limit=abc
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"limit","message":"must be an integer between 1 and 100"})`

#### `API-QUERY-12` — a repeated parameter is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?status=todo&status=done
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"status","message":"must not be repeated"})`

#### `API-QUERY-13` — empty values are rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?status=&limit=
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"status","message":"must be one of: todo, in_progress, done"},{"field":"limit","message":"must be an integer between 1 and 100"})`

#### `API-QUERY-14` — an empty item inside a list is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?status=todo,,done
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"status","message":"must be one of: todo, in_progress, done"})`

#### `API-QUERY-15` — values are case-sensitive
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?status=TODO&order=DESC
- then:
  - status 400
  - body is `<invalid-query body>({"field":"status","message":"must be one of: todo, in_progress, done"},{"field":"order","message":"must be one of: asc, desc"})`

#### `API-QUERY-16` — unknown parameter names are ignored
- given: (default)
- when: GET /tasks?foo=bar&Status=closed
- then:
  - status 200
  - body is exactly `{"items":[],"total":0,"limit":20,"offset":0}`

### Request Rejection

**Common given:** the service is running against `migrated-db`.

#### `API-REJECT-01` — unavailable database returns 503
- given: (default), and the service runs with `ENABLE_TEST_ROUTES=true`, `DATABASE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1` and `DATABASE_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECS=1`, and a `GET /__test/slow?ms=4000&hold_db=true` request is in flight holding the pool's only connection
- when: GET /tasks
- then:
  - status 503
  - body is exactly `{"error":{"code":"service_unavailable","message":"Database temporarily unavailable, please retry","details":[]}}`
  - the response arrives within 2.5 seconds of sending the request

#### `API-REJECT-02` — a method without a handler is rejected
- given: (default)
- when: PUT /tasks with `Content-Type: application/json` and body `{"title":"x"}`
- then:
  - status 405
  - body is exactly `{"error":{"code":"method_not_allowed","message":"Method not allowed","details":[]}}`
  - `tasks` still holds zero rows

### Performance

#### `API-PERF-01` — filtered, sorted listing stays fast with 10,000 tasks
- given: the service is running against `seeded-10k-db`
- when: send 1,000 sequential GET /tasks?status=todo&sort=due_date&limit=100 requests
- then:
  - every response has status 200
  - every response body `items` has 100 entries
  - the 95th percentile of the response times is below 100 ms
- notes: the PRD names a local release build; a run against a debug build that meets the same bound also satisfies it
